summary:
The CCSDS Recommended Standard for the **Return Operational Control Fields (ROCF)** service of the [Space Link Extension](../ccsds/sle/index.md). ROCF delivers to a mission user the 4-octet Operational Control Fields (OCFs) extracted from the good-quality frames of **one Master Channel or one Virtual Channel** of a TM, AOS or USLP return link. The document notes that the most common OCF payload is the **CLCW** of the Communications Operation Procedure (see [COP-1](../ccsds/cop-1.md)). It can also deliver other control-word types such as the SDLS Frame Security Report. ROCF replaces the separate Rtn MC-OCF and Rtn VC-OCF services of the SLE Reference Model. It is described with RAF and RCF on [SLE return services](../ccsds/sle/return-services.md).

Section 2 explains production: the RFP-FG takes a RAF data channel, keeps only 'good' frames, and demultiplexes by MC and VC. It also covers service management, the delivery modes (timely online, complete online, offline), buffering and security. Section 3 defines the operations. ROCF-BIND carries version number '6'. ROCF-START takes start/stop time, requested-global-VCID, control-word-type ('all control word types', 'clcw' or 'not clcw'), tc-vcid (only for 'clcw': pick the CLCWs that report on one TC Virtual Channel, or 'null' for all of them) and update-mode ('continuous', or 'change-based', which delivers an OCF only when its content changes). The other operations are UNBIND, STOP, TRANSFER-DATA (ERT, antenna-ID, data-link-continuity, private-annotation, OCF data), SYNC-NOTIFY, SCHEDULE-STATUS-REPORT, STATUS-REPORT, GET-PARAMETER and PEER-ABORT. Section 4 gives the provider state machine. The annexes hold the ASN.1 modules, the production status model, the conformance matrix, an index and acronyms.

contents.title: Security Aspects of the ROCF Service

key_points.text: Issue 4 (July 2023) adds support for USLP Transfer Frames plus clarifications and corrections. EC 1 (October 2024) repairs figure 2-3.
ROCF delivers to a mission user all operational control fields from one Master Channel or one Virtual Channel. It merges the Rtn MC-OCF and Rtn VC-OCF services of the SLE Reference Model into one.

The ROCF delivery criteria are: ERT within the start/stop window, SCID and VCID matching the requested global VCID, a matching control word type, and, for CLCWs (control word type '0'), a matching telecommand VC. For 'not clcw' OCFs, the Frame Security Report can be delivered.
The most common OCF payload is the CLCW of the COP, which has no confidentiality protection, so the confidentiality of ROCF data usually depends entirely on the underlying communications service.
Only frames annotated 'good' feed ROCF production: valid Reed-Solomon or LDPC codewords, or a correct FECF for uncoded frames.
The version-number value for the ROCF service defined by this issue is '6'.

The ROCF-START invocation carries invoker-credentials, start-time, stop-time, requested-global-VCID, control-word-type, a conditional tc-vcid and update-mode. The return carries performer-credentials, result and diagnostic.

control-word-type is 'all control word types', 'clcw' (type '0') or 'not clcw'; 'not clcw' is the type to use to obtain FSRs. tc-vcid is present only for 'clcw', and 'null' selects CLCWs for every TC VC.

In update-mode 'continuous' every matching OCF is delivered. In 'change-based' an OCF is delivered only if its content differs from the last one delivered for the same tc-vcid, or if none has been delivered since the most recent START.
ROCF-TRANSFER-DATA carries invoker-credentials, earth-receive-time, antenna-ID, data-link-continuity, private-annotation and the OCF data.

GET-PARAMETER exposes delivery-mode, latency-limit, minimum-reporting-cycle, permitted-global-VCID-set, permitted-control-word-type-set, permitted-tc-vcid-set, permitted-update-mode-set, reporting-cycle, requested-control-word-type, requested-global-VCID, requested-tc-vcid, requested-update-mode, return-timeout-period and transfer-buffer-size.
Annex A defines the common SLE ASN.1 modules plus CCSDS-SLE-TRANSFER-SERVICE-ROCF-STRUCTURES, -ROCF-INCOMING-PDUS and -ROCF-OUTGOING-PDUS.

notes: The slug's 'e1' stands for Editorial Change 1 (October 2024). The Document Control table still calls B-3 the 'Current issue' and B-4 the 'Current update', and its footer reads 'July 2024 / October 2023'; both look like editorial leftovers. PDF pages 1-2 are duplicate covers. The extracted text has 156 form-feed pages (registry: 155); the last one is empty. The printed table of contents loses its titles in the extraction, so the pages were mapped through the printed page labels. Like RCF, the normative USLP reference is issue 2 (732.1-B-2). The structure parallels the RAF and RCF specifications. No individual authors are named. The registry copy was taken from ccsds.org on 2026-11-12.
